# Featured Papers

::: {.grid}

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
#### [Magnetic Johnson noise from arbitrarily shaped conductors: experimental validation of the fluctuation-dissipation finite-element method](<http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.42113v1>)
*S. M. Clayton, Y. J. Kim, T. E. Chupp, A. Epstein, J. M. Feltman, A. Fratangelo, T. M. Ito, I. J. Rhudy, F. H. Sottrel, W. A. Terrano, K. L. Wood* <br>
Measurements obtained using a SQUID gradiometer array demonstrate that finite-element calculations accurately capture both the amplitude and frequency dependence of thermal magnetic noise while illustrating how material properties and conductor shapes influence noise spectra.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
#### [Active mechanics of sea star oocytes](<http://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/k71r-5zgm>)
*Peter J. Foster, Alexandra Zampetaki, Jinghui Liu, Sebastian Fürthauer, and Nikta Fakhri* <br>
Molecular interactions within the actomyosin cortex generate the contractile forces that drive large-scale cell shape changes by translating nanoscale protein dynamics into macroscopic physical transformations.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
#### [Two faces of symmetry match in gear-like coupled rotary motors](<http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39121v1>)
*Sara Iranbakhsh, David A. Sivak* <br>
Coupling strength determines whether symmetry matching enhances or suppresses energy transduction in rotary molecular motors, creating a trade-off where the gear ratio that maximizes output power under tight coupling is also the most vulnerable to slipping under weak coupling.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
#### [A Biophysical Framework for Force-Induced Mitochondrial Branches](<https://www.cell.com/biophysj/fulltext/S0006-3495(26)00744-7?rss=yes>)
*Sheda Ben Nejma, Rajit Narayanan Cheramangalam, Juan C. Landoni, Matthew D. Lycas, Julius Winter, Moumita Das, Suliana Manley* <br>
Pulling-induced branches form more frequently at narrower angles and deform parent organelles compared to fusion-based branches, with their short lifetimes regulated by microtubule stability and motor protein dynamics.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
#### [Extraordinary stiffening and reciprocal control in a DNA condensate/actin composite](<http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.38504v1>)
*Sam Wilken, Austin Hopkins, Kyu Hwan Choi, John Berezney, Matthew E. Helgeson, M. Cristina Marchetti, Sho Takatori, Zvonimir Dogic, Omar A. Saleh* <br>
Penetration and entrainment of actin filaments within phase-separated DNA droplets enlarges the effective inclusions to build a dominating contact network, driving a reversible 25-fold increase in matrix stiffness at filler volume fractions below ten percent.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
#### [Optimizing Evolution Under Cyclic Selection: the Case of B Cells](<http://arxiv.org/abs/2610.36596v1>)
*Xingjian Hou, Colin Scheibner, Ned S. Wingreen* <br>
Restricting mutations to the final cell division before selection yields faster evolutionary adaptation than mutating during every division when selection intervals are long, while the optimal adaptation velocity remains nearly invariant to the number of intervening divisions.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
#### [Septin binding restricts                     Shigella                     growth and triggers intracellular tolerance](<https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2529720123>)
*Gizem Özbaykal Güler, Chen Zhang, Dominik Brokatzky, Rajdeep Das, Richard Wheeler, Ivo Gomperts Boneca, Teresa Cortes, Suliana Manley, Serge Mostowy* <br>
Circumferentially oriented septin filaments inhibit bacterial growth by hyperpolarizing *Shigella* cell membranes, forcing the pathogen to deploy the effector OspC1 and stress regulator *cspC* to withstand host cell-autonomous immunity.
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-6}
#### [In vitro binding energies capture Klf4 occupancy across the human genome](<https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2538133123>)
*Anne Schwager, Jonas Neipel, Yahor Savich, Douglas Diehl, Frank Jülicher, Anthony A. Hyman, Stephan W. Grill* <br>
An Ising-based statistical mechanics model of coupled nucleotide recognition, parameterized solely by in vitro binding measurements, accurately predicts Klf4 genomic occupancy without requiring additional fitting parameters.
:::

:::

Fish align their movements with whichever single neighbor exerts the strongest influence at a given moment rather than defaulting to the closest individual.
